summary.text: Sherrod Brown is the Democratic nominee in Ohio's 2026 U.S. Senate special election and a former three-term U.S. senator (2007-2025). A Mansfield native, he served in the Ohio House, as secretary of state and in the U.S. House before winning his Senate seat in 2006; he lost re-election to Bernie Moreno in 2024. His campaign says he is running on his record of fighting for Ohio workers and the dignity of work.

paragraphs.text: Brown was born in Mansfield, Ohio, where his campaign says he was born and raised. He earned a bachelor's degree in Russian studies from Yale University in 1974 and a graduate degree in education from Ohio State University in 1981.
He taught at Ohio State University's Mansfield campus from 1979 to 1981, and served as a state representative in the Ohio House from 1975 to 1982.
Brown served as Ohio Secretary of State from 1983 to 1991 and then won election to represent Ohio's 13th Congressional District in the U.S. House, serving from 1993 to 2007.
In 2006 he was elected to the U.S. Senate, defeating incumbent Mike DeWine, and he won re-election in 2012, defeating Josh Mandel, and in 2018, defeating Jim Renacci.
He lost his 2024 re-election bid to Bernie Moreno, 50.1% to 46.5%.
Brown is running in the special election for the remaining two years of the term J.D. Vance won in 2022, against Republican Sen. Jon Husted, who was appointed to the seat in January 2025.
According to his campaign website, he lives in Columbus with his wife, Connie Schultz, a Pulitzer Prize-winning columnist and author; they have three daughters, a son and eight grandchildren.
